entries.title: Romans 11:1
segments: The tribe of Benjamin. The tribes of Judah and Benjamin remained faithful to the House of David.  Jerusalem was in the territory of the tribe of Benjamin.

entries.title: Romans 11:2
segments: Which he foreknew. And included in His purpose to have mercy upon all (
).  See notes on

entries.title: Romans 11:4
segments: Baal. The Sun god or chief deity of the Canaanites.  'Baal' means lord.  Each locality had its special Baal, and the various local Baals were summed up under the name of Baalim, 'lords.'

entries.title: Romans 11:5
segments:
Remnant. The Jews who had accepted Christ.  Paul aims in this chapter to show that the rejection of the Jews was only temporary.  Some had been faithful and even the great majority, though they had rejected Christ, were not finally cast off.  The Gentiles had been admitted to the place in God's favor, which the chosen people might have had.  Influenced by Gentile example, the Jews would yet accept Christ.
 

 
The election of grace. Chosen by the favor of God apart from merit or works.

entries.title: Romans 11:6
segments: Otherwise grace is no more grace. That is, if it can be earned and demanded as a debt.

entries.title: Romans 11:7
segments:
That which Israel seeketh for, that he obtained not. Because righteousness was attempted as a task instead of being accepted by faith as the gift of God.
 

 
Election. See

.
 

 
Were hardened. By their own faults.

entries.title: Romans 11:8
segments: A spirit of stupor. By their failure in faith they had become spiritually insensible.

entries.title: Romans 11:9
segments:
A snare and a trap. The spiritual self-sufficiency, ending in unbelief and worldliness, which had resulted from the Jews trusting in the mere possession of the law and its ordinances.
 

 
Recompense. Penalty.

entries.title: Romans 11:11
segments:
Did they stumble that they might fall? The question here implies that the stumbling did not and could not end in a final fall; their temporary fall due to their rejection of Christ resulted in the salvation of the Gentiles.
 

 
Jealousy. Ending in the desire to emulate the Gentiles in willingness to accept Christ.

entries.title: Romans 11:12
segments: Their fullness. The salvation by faith of the whole Jewish people.

entries.title: Romans 11:13
segments:
,14
 
I speak to you that are Gentiles. In these two verses Paul's intention is to remind the Gentiles that what he wrote about the Jews has an application to them also.  He rejoices in the probability that, by reason of the Gentiles, people of his own race may be saved.

entries.title: Romans 11:15
segments: Reconciling of the world. See

.
 

 
Life from the dead. Their salvation by faith would be spiritual life, or as a resurrection from the dead compared with their former condition.

entries.title: Romans 11:16
segments: First fruit. See

.  The first fruits were Abraham and the other Jewish patriarchs.
 

 
Holy. Here to be taken in the sense of being set apart, dedicated to God.

entries.title: Romans 11:17
segments: Thou, being a wild olive, etc.  Referring to the Gentiles, who were without the special favor, which God had shown to the Jews, and were therefore a worthless branch of wild olive in comparison with the real olive tree.

entries.title: Romans 11:18
segments: Glory not over the branches. Do not be proud and scornful toward the Jews because you have gained their place in God's favor.

entries.title: Romans 11:21
segments: Neither will he spare thee. A warning to the Gentiles in the church at Rome and other places to continue in faith.

entries.title: Romans 11:23
segments: Shall be grafted in. Saved by faith.

entries.title: Romans 11:26
segments: The Deliverer. See

entries.title: Romans 11:27
segments: When I shall take away their sins. A covenant of forgiveness of sins as contrasted with a covenant under which laws were to be obeyed.

entries.title: Romans 11:28
segments:
As touching the gospel. In regard to God's purpose in spreading the gospel.
 

 
Enemies. Punished as enemies for their rejection of Christ.
 

 
Election. God's favor to them as the chosen people.
 

 
The fathers' sake. The patriarchs; the great ancestors.

entries.title: Romans 11:29
segments: Not repented of. That is, God's purpose of mercy in regard to the Jews remains the same.

entries.title: Romans 11:30
segments:
,31
 
But now have obtained mercy. The disobedience of both Jews and Gentiles is emphasized in order to bring out more clearly their deliverance through God's mercy.  The fact that Jews were especially favored did not in this respect put them in a more advantageous position than Gentiles.

entries.title: Romans 11:32
segments:
God hath shut up all unto disobedience. 'All' here has no reference to individuals, but to the great mass of Jews and Gentiles, collectively considered, who have rejected God's goodness.
 

 
That he might have mercy upon all. Here appears the divine purpose from the beginning.  The penalties of disobedience were inflicted only to make the divine mercy supremely manifest.  The Jews were first favored by God, but fell away from Him; the Gentiles had also fallen away through neglecting the light of conscience within them, but afterwards heard the divine message and received salvation.  But in all God's discipline of both Jews and Gentiles His supreme purpose was to have mercy upon them.

entries.title: Romans 11:33
segments: Unsearchable. Not to be fully understood and explained.

entries.title: Romans 11:35
segments: Who hath first given to him, etc.  Who hath laid God under any obligation?  God's mercy without man's merit is the underlying truth.
